A Valve - Electro-Hydraulic Servo is a type of industrial valve that uses hydraulic fluid to control the flow of fluid in a system. It consists of several components that work together to regulate the flow of fluid. The main components of a Valve - Electro-Hydraulic Servo asset include:

1. Valve body or cylinder: This is the main housing for the valve's components. It is typically made of metal and has a cylindrical shape. The valve body provides a chamber for the piston to move up and down, and it has holes for the inlet and outlet of fluid.
2. Piston: The piston is a movable component that is inserted into the valve body. It is used to control the flow of fluid by blocking or unblocking the holes in the valve body. The piston is typically made of metal and has a smooth surface to minimize friction.
3. O-rings: O-rings are used to seal the piston and prevent leakage of hydraulic fluid. They are placed between the piston and the valve body, and they provide a tight seal to ensure that fluid does not escape.
4. Position springs: Position springs are used to return the piston to its original position when the hydraulic pressure is released. They are typically made of metal and are designed to provide a consistent force to push the piston back to its starting position.
5. Coil: The coil is an electrical component that is used to generate a magnetic field. The magnetic field is used to control the movement of the piston. The coil is typically made of copper wire and is wrapped around a core.
6. Electrical wiring and connections: The electrical wiring and connections are used to connect the coil to a power source and control system. The control system sends electrical signals to the coil, which generates a magnetic field that moves the piston and controls the flow of fluid in the system.
7. Actuator: The actuator is the component that converts the electrical signal into mechanical movement. It is typically a solenoid coil that is connected to the piston. When the electrical signal is applied to the coil, it generates a magnetic field that moves the piston up or down.
8. Limit switch: The limit switch is a mechanical component that provides a signal to the control system when the piston reaches its maximum position. It is typically a microswitch that is activated by a lever or cam attached to the piston.
9. Pressure gauge: The pressure gauge is a mechanical component that measures the pressure of the hydraulic fluid in the system. It is typically a dial gauge that shows the pressure reading.
10. Safety relief valve: The safety relief valve is a mechanical component that is designed to release excess pressure in the system. It is typically a spring-loaded valve that opens when the pressure exceeds a certain level.
